newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen up $0.50-$1 -dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen up $0.50-$1 -dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt higher as hog marketings continue to drop from the large numbers seen early in the week, livestock dealers said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to plants in Iowa/southern Minnesota direct trade could range from $53.00 to $53.50 as packers bid higher in attempts to draw more hogs to market.
Illinois top prices at the plant door could span $52.50 to $53.50, the dealers said.
"Marketings almost came to a complete stop," one central Illinois hog buyer said of Wednesday's sparse run.
Indiana/Ohio hog buyers said top prices at the plant could range from $52.50 to $53.00, possibly reaching $53.50, following a sharp decline in hog movement at mid-week.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts Tuesday were tabbed by USDA at 100,000 head, compared with that day's estimate of 112,000, according to USDA. Wednesday's estimate was 105,000 head.

Marketings early in the week were heavy as hogs held back by last week's cold and snow in the Midwest came to market. Light movement now was seen as an indication producers were becoming more current in their marketings, dealers said.
